prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
Done. One small cleanup: the `popped` counter is incremented via a function-reassignment hack that works but is ugly. It's functional, so I'll leave it — the game works.

**[goal]** Win95-style archery balloon-pop level in `./game/index.html`, single file, no build step.

**[action]** Wrote one self-contained HTML file: canvas renderer, WebAudio synth (no assets), mouse/touch input. Archer on the left aims with the mouse; hold to draw (power bar fills, bow string pulls back, dotted trajectory preview shows the arc), release to fire a gravity-affected arrow. Balloons drift up at varied sizes — small = 3 pts, medium = 2, large = 1, with a combo multiplier. Pop = burst particles + expanding ring + screen shake + white flash + "+N" float. HUD: score, goal, timer, accuracy, power bar. States: title (click to start), play, win (10 pts in 60 s), lose (time out). All sounds synthesized: draw whoosh, release thump, pop (pitch drop + noise burst), win arpeggio, lose descending tone. Press Start 2P font from Google Fonts for the '95 look.

**[result]** Verified live in the browser: title screen renders, game starts on click, balloons spawn and drift, trajectory preview guides aiming, a shot popped a balloon (SCORE 1, ACC 50%, pop ring + confetti + "+1" visible on screen). Browser tab closed.

**[next]** Assumptions stated: "a way to lose" = fail to reach 10 points before the 60 s timer ends (no lives); "first level" = a single self-contained level, no progression. Opened the file once, played, confirmed hit/score/pop feedback, closed the tab. How I know it's right: I observed the actual rendered frames — title, in-play HUD, arrow in flight, and a successful pop with score increment — not just that the file loads.
